::: {.eyebrow}
Case 06 · Subseasonal · Weekly rainfall · Full Indonesia
:::

On **Wednesday 1 November 2023** the GEFSv12 run started at 00 UTC gives a forecaster
the next four weeks: **week 1** (2-8 November), **week 2** (9-15), **week 3**
(16-22), **week 4** (23-29), and **weeks 3-4** together (16-29 November), the period
of NOAA CPC's [week 3-4 outlook](https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/predictions/WK34/).
This case calibrates that run with CCA and PCR through CPT, shows what it said
against what happened, and measures how far each lead can be trusted.

It is the same moment as the [monthly](monthly-leads-2023.qmd) and
[seasonal](seasonal-leads-2023.qmd) cases, one step closer in time. Every map works
at CHIRPS v3.0's native 0.05° grid: 61,190 pixels over Indonesia. All numbers come
from the [executed notebook](../notebooks/week-leads-2023.ipynb).

Hover, tap or use the arrow keys on any map or chart to read values; each view can
be downloaded as it is set. Maps load when you choose them, one small file per map.

::: {.callout-note title="The short result"}
- **The forecast of 1 November leaned dry, and the weeks were dry.** Weeks 1 to 3
  came in at 45-47 mm over Indonesia against normals of 63-70 mm. Week 1 was
  forecast at 48.9 mm (CCA); weeks 2 and 3 were forecast closer to normal, at 53.1
  and 61.3 mm.
- **Placing the categories was harder:** for every lead the hit rate of the most
  likely category was below that of always forecasting the category that turned out
  most common, picked with hindsight, by 0.8 to 6.9 points.
- **How far to trust each lead**, from all October-December weeks of 2000-2018: the
  area-mean CCA correlation is 0.35 for week 1, 0.29 for week 2, 0.26 for week 3,
  0.17 for week 4, and 0.26 for weeks 3-4 together. The raw GEFSv12 correlation is
  higher for weeks 1 and 2 (0.50 and 0.34) and level from week 3.
:::

## The forecast issued on 1 November 2023

A forecast is issued at 00 UTC on a Wednesday. Model day *d* covers roughly the same
24 hours as observed day issue + *d*, so each lead is a window of days after the
issue date. The menus start at this forecast and add the five later Wednesdays,
up to 6 December 2023, the last whose five leads all fall in October-December, the
period forecast and verified here.

::: {.story-interactive}
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof timelineIssue = selectControl("Issue date", issueChoices, "2023-11-01")
weekIssueTimeline(weekData, timelineIssue)
```
:::

Each map is one lead against its own target, week 1 at the top. Switch between the
forecast, the observation, their difference and the categories, or pick another
issue date.

::: {.story-interactive}
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof mapIssue = selectControl("Issue date", issueChoices, "2023-11-01")
viewof issueMethod = selectControl("Calibration", [["CCA", "CCA"], ["PCR", "PCR"]], "CCA")
viewof issueView = selectControl("Show", [["total", "Forecast total"], ["observed", "Observed total"], ["difference", "Forecast minus observed"], ["category", "Most likely category"], ["observedCategory", "Observed category"]], "total")
weekIssueMaps(weekData, geo, mapIssue, issueMethod, issueView)
```
:::

| Lead | Target | Forecast (mm) | Observed (mm) | 2000-2018 mean (mm) | Observed below / near / above normal (% of area) | Hit rate (%) | Reference (%) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Week 1 | 2-8 Nov | 48.9 | 46.2 | 63.0 | 52.4 / 40.0 / 7.6 | 51.0 | 52.4 |
| Week 2 | 9-15 Nov | 53.1 | 44.9 | 65.7 | 58.6 / 31.7 / 9.7 | 57.8 | 58.6 |
| Week 3 | 16-22 Nov | 61.3 | 47.0 | 69.8 | 68.3 / 20.5 / 11.2 | 63.8 | 68.3 |
| Week 4 | 23-29 Nov | 67.4 | 66.8 | 69.7 | 35.2 / 36.4 / 28.3 | 34.0 | 36.4 |
| Weeks 3-4 | 16-29 Nov | 131.2 | 113.8 | 139.6 | 54.5 / 31.8 / 13.7 | 47.6 | 54.5 |

: CCA forecast issued 1 November 2023, area-weighted over Indonesia. Source: [issued-2023-11-01.csv](../data/week-leads-2023/issued-2023-11-01.csv), which also has PCR.

- **Amounts.** The first three weeks of November were dry: 45-47 mm against
  normals of 63-70 mm. The forecast for week 1 was close (48.9 against 46.2 mm).
  Further ahead it moved towards the normal (53.1 mm for week 2, 61.3 mm for week 3)
  and so missed more of the dry spell. A regression forecast moves towards the
  normal as its skill falls, which is what the skill section below measures. Week 4
  returned to near normal (66.8 mm) and was forecast almost exactly (67.4 mm).
- **Categories.** For weeks 1-3 the forecast made below normal the most likely
  category over 84% to 96% of the area, and below normal was observed over 52% to
  68%. Its hit rate (51% to 64%) stayed under the **reference**, always forecasting
  the category that turned out most common, chosen with hindsight, by 0.8 to 4.5
  points; for weeks 3-4 together the gap was 6.9 points (47.6% against 54.5%). For
  week 4 the forecast favoured above normal over 55% of the area in a week that was
  mixed; its hit rate was 34% against 36%.

One issue date is one outcome per lead. The next sections show how well each lead
does on average.

## How far each lead can be trusted

The calibration of each lead is trained and scored on every week starting on a
Thursday in October-December 2000-2018, 249 targets per lead. GEFSv12's hindcasts
start on Wednesdays, like the real-time forecast, so training uses exactly the same
leads as real use. CCA (3 predictor and 3 predictand EOFs, 2 CCA modes) and PCR
(3 predictor EOFs) are fitted through `cptcore`, the layer PyCPT's `evaluate_models`
calls, with cross-validation leaving out 27 targets at a time (the held-out week and
13 on each side, about a season). At 0.05° one fit took 76 to 90 minutes for CCA and
23 to 26 minutes for PCR, so the ten fits ran in parallel. For every fit, CPT's
correlation map equals the correlation recomputed from its own cross-validated
hindcasts to within 0.000001.

**Pearson correlation** is 0 for no linear relationship; **2AFC** is the chance
that the forecast ranks two different weeks in the observed order, 50% for no
skill [(Mason and Weigel 2009)](https://doi.org/10.1175/2008MWR2553.1).

::: {.story-interactive}
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof skillMetric = selectControl("Score", [["Pearson", "Pearson correlation"], ["2AFC (%)", "2AFC"]], "Pearson")
skillByLead(weekData, skillMetric)
```
:::

| Lead | CCA Pearson | PCR Pearson | Raw GEFS Pearson | CCA 2AFC (%) | PCR 2AFC (%) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Week 1 | 0.35 | 0.36 | 0.50 | 62.8 | 63.1 |
| Week 2 | 0.29 | 0.28 | 0.34 | 60.3 | 60.3 |
| Week 3 | 0.26 | 0.26 | 0.25 | 59.6 | 59.6 |
| Week 4 | 0.17 | 0.18 | 0.18 | 56.7 | 56.8 |
| Weeks 3-4 | 0.26 | 0.26 | 0.25 | 59.6 | 59.7 |

: Area-weighted means over 61,190 pixels, 249 targets of 2000-2018. Source: [skill-by-lead.csv](../data/week-leads-2023/skill-by-lead.csv).

1. **Skill falls with lead, most between weeks 3 and 4.** CCA's mean correlation
   drops by 0.06 from week 1 to 2, 0.02 from week 2 to 3, and 0.09 from week 3 to 4.
2. **Two weeks together hold up better than the second of them.** Weeks 3-4 score
   0.26, close to week 3 and well above week 4 alone (0.17).
3. **Calibration does not beat the raw model.** GEFSv12's own anomaly correlates
   better in weeks 1 and 2 (by 0.15 and 0.05 over CCA) and about equally from
   week 3. The calibrated scores pay a cross-validation cost
   [(Barnston and van den Dool 1993)](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0442(1993)006%3C0963:ADICVS%3E2.0.CO;2)
   and see the model only through 3 EOF patterns; neither effect was measured here.
4. **CCA and PCR are nearly identical**, within 0.01 at every lead.

viewof mapMetric = selectControl("Score", mapMethod === "raw" ? [["pearson", "Pearson correlation"]] : [["pearson", "Pearson correlation"], ["twoafc", "2AFC"]], "pearson")

## The whole season: October-December 2023

Every week of October-December 2023 is forecast at every lead, so the scores below
also use the Wednesdays of September and December whose forecasts reach into the
season only in part: sixteen issue dates in all, from 13 September to 27 December.
Over the 13 targets of each lead, scored over every pixel and target
(area-weighted):

| Lead | Method | Hit rate (%) | Reference (%) | RPSS 2023 | RMSE 2023 (mm) | Mean forecast (mm) | Observed mean (mm) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Week 1 | CCA | 50.4 | 49.4 | 0.12 | 28.6 | 55.7 | 51.1 |
| Week 1 | PCR | 49.5 | 49.4 | 0.12 | 28.8 | 55.7 | 51.1 |
| Week 2 | CCA | 50.2 | 49.4 | 0.12 | 28.5 | 56.0 | 51.1 |
| Week 2 | PCR | 49.6 | 49.4 | 0.11 | 28.7 | 55.7 | 51.1 |
| Week 3 | CCA | 46.8 | 49.4 | 0.07 | 29.7 | 58.0 | 51.1 |
| Week 3 | PCR | 45.9 | 49.4 | 0.07 | 29.7 | 57.8 | 51.1 |
| Week 4 | CCA | 45.6 | 49.4 | 0.08 | 29.8 | 57.8 | 51.1 |
| Week 4 | PCR | 44.8 | 49.4 | 0.07 | 30.0 | 57.7 | 51.1 |
| Weeks 3-4 | CCA | 53.2 | 52.2 | 0.14 | 48.3 | 117.5 | 106.5 |
| Weeks 3-4 | PCR | 51.1 | 52.2 | 0.13 | 48.7 | 117.4 | 106.5 |

: October-December 2023. Source: [ond-2023-weekly-forecasts.csv](../data/week-leads-2023/ond-2023-weekly-forecasts.csv).

- **Hit rate** against the **reference**, always forecasting the most frequent
  observed category (below normal, 49.4% of one-week pixel-targets and 52.2% for
  weeks 3-4): weeks 1, 2 and 3-4 matched it to within about a point; weeks 3 and 4
  fell 2.5 to 4.5 points short.
- **RPSS 2023** compares the forecast probabilities with climatological odds
  (33/34/33%) using the ranked probability score
  [(Epstein 1969)](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0450(1969)008%3C0985:ASSFPF%3E2.0.CO;2):
  positive at every lead, highest for weeks 3-4 and weeks 1-2. One season of
  13 weeks rewards leaning the right way in 2023, not skill in general.
- **The totals were too wet** on average: 55.7 to 58.0 mm a week against an observed
  51.1 mm, although the most likely category was below normal over 58% to 73% of
  the area.

## Observations and anomalies

The observations are **daily CHIRPS v3.0** (the `rnl` variant), exported for
Indonesia from Earth Engine and converted to yearly NetCDF files by the tutorial's
[`gee_daily_to_netcdf.py`](https://github.com/bennyistanto/pycpt-tutorial/blob/main/research/scripts/gee_daily_to_netcdf.py).
Their sums over three dekads (2005, 2012 and 2023) equal the dekadal archive used by
the other cases to within 0.0001 mm at every Indonesian pixel, with the same missing
pixels. A weekly total is the sum of its seven days (14 for weeks 3-4).

::: {.callout-warning title="Daily CHIRPS is not an independent daily product"}
CHC builds daily CHIRPS v3.0 from the pentad product: each pentad's amount is shared
between its days using the timing of ERA5 (the `rnl` variant used here) or IMERG,
with no separate daily station blending, and CHC recommends pentadal or longer
totals wherever the science allows
([CHIRPS daily readme](https://data.chc.ucsb.edu/products/CHIRPS/v3.0/daily/readme.txt)).
These weeks run Thursday to Wednesday and so cut across pentads: how much of a
pentad's rain falls inside a week comes from ERA5's timing, not from stations. The
weekly totals, and the skill measured against them, carry that dependence; how much
it matters was not measured here. The same readme notes that the daily dates follow
ERA5's UTC days (00 to 00 UTC), while the stations behind the pentad totals do not
all report on UTC days, so the match with GEFSv12's model days is approximate. The
[pentad case](pentad-leads-2023.qmd) uses the pentad product itself.
:::

Rainfall rises through October-December, so model and observations are turned into
**anomalies** before fitting. A target's mean is the average of 19 training targets
of the same lead, one from each year 2000-2018: the one starting closest to the same
day of the season (on average 1.7 days away, at most 6). Each forecast **total** is
that mean for the observations plus the calibrated anomaly, set to zero where the sum
is negative. The 2000-2018 mean over Indonesian pixels is 64.1 mm a week (129.2 mm
for weeks 3-4).

## What this does and does not show

This is one model, one set of fixed settings, 19 training years and one verifying
season, with the headline on one issue date. It shows that, for GEFSv12 weekly
rainfall over Indonesia in October-December, skill falls from 0.35 to 0.17 over four
weeks, that combining weeks 3 and 4 keeps more skill than week 4 alone, and that
calibration with these settings did not add to the raw model's correlation. The
observations are retrospective CHIRPS v3.0, not what was available when each
forecast was issued, and the 2023 forecasts average 31 GEFSv12 members while the
hindcasts have 11.

The [dekad case](dekad-leads-2023.qmd) asks the same question by dekad, issued on
31 October 2023.
